card.title: Half a Beat Late
card.instruction: Use the group’s reactions as your cue, joining each one a moment late and escalating your enthusiasm to stay included.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on the new dragon! I was just about to clap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were gasping. It ate the shed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes! A devastating shed. I mean devastating loss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Checking whether we've moved into brave celebration yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Room on your blanket? Oh, everyone's cheering! Come on, Tigers! Best team in the county!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ooh, poor keeper. That's my daughter limping off. Hold her water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, poor love! I'll carry her bag too. She can have my chair!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's waving us back! Yes! That's my girl! She's staying in goal!

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, yes! Tigers forever! Can I join you every Saturday? I'll buy a season ticket!

mechanism: A follows each group reaction just late, enlarging cheering, concern and renewed cheering to secure a place with the spectators.
confusable: Unlike covering one social mistake with a confident excuse, A must actually join changing group reactions and escalate participation.
comparison: The recovered sports alternative follows live concern and renewed pride in a player; the mirror alternative follows laughter, rescue alarm and gratitude.
